沙市堂 主日崇拜 · Shashi Church Sunday Worship

2026年9月20日（主日）· Sunday 20 September 2026 · 上午 9:00
主礼 Presiding: 张强 传道 (evangelist) · 证道 Sermon: 彭金文 牧师 (pastor)
晚堂 Evening service 19:00 at 香榭丽都聚会点 (meeting point, 江津中路): 主礼 丁志云 传道 · 证道 彭金文 牧师

今日主题 · Today’s Theme

饶恕 forgiveness — and the shared life of 神的选民, God’s chosen people. Every text today circles one question: what does it look like to live as people who have already been forgiven? The service answers in an arc.

1. God’s character first. The call to worship (诗篇 103) quotes God’s own self-description to Moses on Sinai: 有怜悯，有恩典，不轻易发怒，且有丰盛的慈爱 — merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love. He does not keep accusing, does not repay us as our sins deserve, and removes our 过犯 as far as east from west. Forgiveness is not first a duty laid on us; it is what God is like.

2. Three angles on the same command (the responsive lessons). 约瑟 Joseph (创世记 50) forgives the brothers who sold him, because he refuses to stand in God’s place (我岂能代替神呢) and can see God’s good purpose inside their evil (你们的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的). 保罗 Paul (罗马书 14) tells a church divided over food and holy days to stop 论断 judging and 轻看 despising one another: each of us is the Lord’s servant and will answer to him alone. 耶稣 Jesus (马太福音 18) tells 彼得 Peter that forgiveness has no ceiling — 七十个七次 — and the parable’s absurd arithmetic (10,000 talents against 100 denarii) shows why: what God has forgiven us dwarfs anything we are asked to forgive.

3. The way of life (歌罗西书 3:12–17, the sermon text). Because you are 选民、圣洁、蒙爱 — chosen, holy, beloved — 穿上 put on 怜悯、恩慈、谦虚、温柔、忍耐; 彼此包容，彼此饶恕 bear with and forgive one another, 主怎样饶恕了你们，你们也要怎样饶恕人 as the Lord forgave you; and over everything 爱心 love, 联络全德 the belt that holds the rest together. Verses 15–17 then describe a community wearing those clothes: 基督的平安 the peace of Christ as umpire in your hearts, 基督的道理 the word of Christ dwelling richly through 诗章、颂词、灵歌 singing, and everything done 奉主耶稣的名 in Jesus’ name with 感谢 thanksgiving. The preacher’s three points follow Paul’s order — 身份 identity → 品格 character → 团契 fellowship — so listen for those three words.

4. The music carries the same thread. Hymn 23 gives thanks for 救赎 redemption; the creed confesses 罪得赦免 the forgiveness of sins; the anthem sings 1 Corinthians 13’s definition of a love that 不计算人的恶 keeps no record of wrongs; hymn 250 draws nearer to the cross where the debt was cancelled; hymn 357 says 崇拜才能尽虔诚 worship is only complete when we love each other; and the Lord’s Prayer asks 免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债.

Why it fits this church. 饶恕 forgiveness and 包容 bearing-with are the practical glue of a congregation; the word the 和合本 uses for what Christ did for us — 饶恕 — is the very word we are told to do for each other. If you remember one sentence from today: 主怎样饶恕了你们，你们也要怎样饶恕人 (Col 3:13).

Lectionary note: the four readings are the Revised Common Lectionary set for Year A, Proper 19, which is why they share one theme; Colossians 3 is the church’s own choice of sermon text.

逐项解读 · Walk-Through ↑

1 · 序乐 Prelude — 众立·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Silence first. 安静 — the service begins by listening, not speaking; the next item says why.

Organ/piano prelude while the 诗班 (choir), 主礼人 (presider) and 证道人 (preacher) process in. Everyone stands and keeps silent. Hymns come from《赞美诗（新编）》— the Chinese New Hymnal (China Christian Council, 1983, 400 hymns; hymnals are usually in the pews and lyrics with 简谱 numbered notation are projected). Numbers are announced as 赞美诗第 … 首 (“hymn number …”).

2 · 问安 Greeting — 赞美诗 396《主在圣殿中》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Habakkuk 2:20 sits in a chapter where God judges the violent and vindicates the faithful: the Lord is in his temple means he is the judge — so we need not be (Joseph: “am I in the place of God?”; Paul: “who are you to judge another’s servant?”).

♪ 五线谱 score →

Sung softly as an introit (哈巴谷书 Habakkuk 2:20). Music by George F. Root (1820–1895, the American composer of “The Battle Cry of Freedom”); taken into the 1936 Hymns of Universal Praise (普天颂赞) and then the 1983 hymnal. After it the presider usually greets: 弟兄姊妹，主内平安！ Brothers and sisters, peace in the Lord! — the congregation answers 平安！.

主在圣殿中，主在圣殿中，普天下的人，在主面前都应当肃静，肃静，肃静，应当肃静。阿们。
The Lord is in His holy temple, the Lord is in His holy temple; let all the earth keep silence, let all the earth keep silence before Him; keep silence, keep silence before Him. Amen.

20 惟耶和华在他的圣殿中；全地的人都当在他面前肃敬静默。
20 But Yahweh is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him!

3 · 宣召 Call to Worship — 诗篇 Psalm 103:8–12 · 众立 ↑

主题 Theme: The theme stated at the start, as God does it: slow to anger, not repaying, removing sin infinitely far. Everything that follows asks us to do the same.

8 耶和华有怜悯，有恩典，不轻易发怒，且有丰盛的慈爱。
8 Yahweh is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness.
9 他不长久责备，也不永远怀怒。
9 He will not always accuse; neither will he stay angry forever.
10 他没有按我们的罪过待我们，也没有照我们的罪孽报应我们。
10 He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities.
11 天离地何等的高，他的慈爱向敬畏他的人也是何等的大！
11 For as the heavens are high above the earth, so great is his loving kindness toward those who fear him.
12 东离西有多远，他叫我们的过犯离我们也有多远！
12 As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.

背景 Background. A psalm of David (大卫的诗) about God’s 慈爱 (hesed, steadfast covenant love). Verse 8 quotes God’s own self-description to Moses on Sinai (出 Exodus 34:6: “merciful and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love”). Four pictures of forgiveness follow: God does not keep accusing (v. 9), does not repay us as our sins deserve (v. 10), his love is as high as the heavens (v. 11, vertical), and he removes our 过犯 (transgressions) as far as east from west (v. 12, horizontal — two directions that never meet, i.e. infinitely far). It sets the day’s theme: God’s forgiveness is both the model and the ground for ours.

4 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 23《赞美歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Thanksgiving for 救赎 redemption (stanza 1: “completed our redemption for us”). The forgiven people — Col 3:12 “holy and beloved” — begin by bringing thanks; Col 3:15–17 will say 感谢 be thankful three times.

♪ 五线谱 score →

“We Praise Thee, O God, Our Redeemer, Creator.” Words by Julia Cady Cory (1882–1963), written in 1902 at the request of the organist of Brick Presbyterian Church, New York, for Thanksgiving (the hymnal dates it c. 1910). Tune KREMSER, a Dutch folk melody (Valerius, 1626; arr. Eduard Kremser 1877) — the same tune as “We Gather Together.” Chinese translation 杨旅复, 1982, for the New Hymnal. Section: 崇敬颂赞·圣父 (Adoration — God the Father). 3/4 time, D major.

1. 赞美上帝，为我们完成了救赎，我众来到主面前，献上礼物；虔诚供奉主前，屈膝敬拜不止，来感谢主圣名，欢唱赞美主。
2. 先贤之神，恳求你听我们倾诉，蒙主引导经试炼，风波安渡；每当患难临头，主必引领出险，生活能够得胜，全靠主帮助。
3. 敬献颂赞，有救主为我们引路，真诚感谢颂扬主，我众欢呼；因主在我身旁，有主膀臂护卫，我们感谢歌唱，永远赞美主。阿们。

1. We praise Thee, O God, our Redeemer, Creator; in grateful devotion our tribute we bring. We lay it before Thee, we kneel and adore Thee; we bless Thy holy name, glad praises we sing.
2. We worship Thee, God of our fathers, we bless Thee; through life’s storm and tempest our Guide hast Thou been. When perils o’ertake us, escape Thou wilt make us, and with Thy help, O Lord, our battles we win.
3. With voices united our praises we offer, to Thee, great Jehovah, glad anthems we raise. Thy strong arm will guide us, our God is beside us; to Thee, our great Redeemer, forever be praise.

5 · 祷告 Prayer — 众立·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Opening prayer, usually with confession of sin: being forgiven ourselves is where Matthew 18’s “as I had mercy on you” starts.

The presider’s opening prayer (开会祷告 / invocation): praise, confession, and asking God’s presence on the service. Stand quietly; join in the closing 阿们.

6 · 宣信 Confession of Faith — 赞美诗 395《使徒信经》· 众立·同诵 ↑

主题 Theme: Two creed lines carry the day: 我信罪得赦免 the forgiveness of sins and 圣徒相通 the communion of saints — forgiven people, living as one body (Col 3:15).

♪ 五线谱 score →

The Apostles’ Creed, recited together (同诵 — spoken, though hymnal 395 also prints John Stainer’s chant setting, from 普天颂赞).

我信上帝，全能的父，创造天地的主。我信我主耶稣基督，上帝独生的子；因圣灵感孕，由童贞女马利亚所生；在本丢彼拉多手下受难，被钉于十字架，受死，埋葬；降在阴间，第三天从死人中复活；升天，坐在全能父上帝的右边；将来必从那里降临，审判活人死人。我信圣灵；我信圣而公之教会；我信圣徒相通；我信罪得赦免；我信身体复活；我信永生。阿们。

I believe in God, the Father almighty, creator of heaven and earth. I believe in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died, and was buried; he descended to the dead. On the third day he rose again; he ascended into heaven, he is seated at the right hand of the Father, and he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.

Note 上帝 (here) and 神 (in the Bible text below) are both “God” — the two Chinese Protestant conventions; the hymnal uses 上帝, this church’s Bible edition uses 神.

7 · 诗班献唱 Choir Anthem —《爱的真谛》· 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: 1 Cor 13 defines the love that Col 3:14 puts “over all”: 不计算人的恶 keeps no record of wrongs; 凡事包容 bears all things is the same word as 彼此包容 bear with one another in Col 3:13. The choir sings the definition; the sermon applies it.

“The True Meaning of Love” — 哥林多前书 1 Corinthians 13:4–8a set to music by the Taiwanese church composer 简铭耀 (Taiwan Theological College). Probably the best-known Chinese Christian song of all — sung at weddings and in every kind of church. The choir’s text is scripture, so you can follow it exactly (the song says 不计算人家的恶 for 不计算人的恶):

4 爱是恒久忍耐，又有恩慈；爱是不嫉妒；爱是不自夸，不张狂，
4 Love is patient and is kind; love doesn’t envy. Love doesn’t brag, is not proud,
5 不做害羞的事，不求自己的益处，不轻易发怒，不计算人的恶，
5 doesn’t behave itself inappropriately, doesn’t seek its own way, is not provoked, takes no account of evil;
6 不喜欢不义，只喜欢真理；
6 doesn’t rejoice in unrighteousness, but rejoices with the truth;
7 凡事包容，凡事相信，凡事盼望，凡事忍耐。
7 bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
8 爱是永不止息。
8 Love never fails.

8 · 经训 Scripture Lessons — 会众同应 (responsive) ↑

主题 Theme: Three angles on one command: Joseph — forgiveness as trust in God’s providence; Romans 14 — no judging one another over disputable things; Matthew 18 — forgive because you have been forgiven far more.

Three lessons, read responsively: the leader reads a verse and the congregation the next (or the congregation reads together). All three are about forgiveness.

创世记 Genesis 50:15–21 — 约瑟饶恕哥哥们 Joseph forgives his brothers ↑

15 约瑟的哥哥们见父亲死了，就说：「或者约瑟怀恨我们，照着我们从前待他一切的恶足足地报复我们。」
15 When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all the evil which we did to him.”
16 他们就打发人去见约瑟，说：「你父亲未死以先吩咐说：『
16 They sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded before he died, saying,
17 你们要对约瑟这样说：从前你哥哥们恶待你，求你饶恕他们的过犯和罪恶。』如今求你饶恕你父亲神之仆人的过犯。」他们对约瑟说这话，约瑟就哭了。
17 ‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
18 他的哥哥们又来俯伏在他面前，说：「我们是你的仆人。」
18 His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, “Behold, we are your servants.”
19 约瑟对他们说：「不要害怕，我岂能代替神呢？
19 Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?
20 从前你们的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的，要保全许多人的性命，成就今日的光景。
20 As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is today, to save many people alive.
21 现在你们不要害怕，我必养活你们和你们的妇人孩子。」于是约瑟用亲爱的话安慰他们。
21 Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

背景 Background. The last scene of Genesis. Years earlier the brothers sold 约瑟 (Joseph) into slavery (ch. 37); now that their father 雅各 Jacob is dead (50:1–14) they fear delayed revenge. They send a message claiming a dying wish of Jacob’s (which Genesis never records — possibly invented in fear), and offer themselves as slaves. Joseph weeps. His answer has two anchors: “我岂能代替神呢？” Am I in the place of God? — vengeance belongs to God, not to him (cf. 罗 Rom 12:19) — and “你们的意思是要害我，但神的意思原是好的” you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good (v. 20), the theological summit of the Joseph story: God’s providence works through, and over, human evil to “save many lives” (the famine). Forgiveness here is concrete: 不要害怕 “don’t be afraid,” provision for their families, and “kind words” (安慰, lit. speaking to their hearts). Listen for 饶恕 (forgive), 过犯 (transgression), 害怕 (afraid).

罗马书 Romans 14:1–12 — 不要论断弟兄 Do not judge your brother ↑

1 信心软弱的，你们要接纳，但不要辩论所疑惑的事。
1 Now accept one who is weak in faith, but not for disputes over opinions.
2 有人信百物都可吃；但那软弱的，只吃蔬菜。
2 One man has faith to eat all things, but he who is weak eats only vegetables.
3 吃的人不可轻看不吃的人；不吃的人不可论断吃的人；因为神已经收纳他了。
3 Don’t let him who eats despise him who doesn’t eat. Don’t let him who doesn’t eat judge him who eats, for God has accepted him.
4 你是谁，竟论断别人的仆人呢？他或站住或跌倒，自有他的主人在；而且他也必要站住，因为主能使他站住。
4 Who are you who judge another’s servant? To his own lord he stands or falls. Yes, he will be made to stand, for God has power to make him stand.
5 有人看这日比那日强；有人看日日都是一样。只是各人心里要意见坚定。
5 One man esteems one day as more important. Another esteems every day alike. Let each man be fully assured in his own mind.
6 守日的人是为主守的。吃的人是为主吃的，因他感谢神；不吃的人是为主不吃的，也感谢神。
6 He who observes the day, observes it to the Lord; and he who does not observe the day, to the Lord he does not observe it. He who eats, eats to the Lord, for he gives God thanks. He who doesn’t eat, to the Lord he doesn’t eat, and gives God thanks.
7 我们没有一个人为自己活，也没有一个人为自己死。
7 For none of us lives to himself, and none dies to himself.
8 我们若活着，是为主而活；若死了，是为主而死。所以，我们或活或死总是主的人。
8 For if we live, we live to the Lord. Or if we die, we die to the Lord. If therefore we live or die, we are the Lord’s.
9 因此，基督死了，又活了，为要作死人并活人的主。
9 For to this end Christ died, rose, and lived again, that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
10 你这个人，为甚么论断弟兄呢？又为甚么轻看弟兄呢？因我们都要站在神的台前。
10 But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you again, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.
11 经上写着：主说：我凭着我的永生起誓：万膝必向我跪拜；万口必向我承认。
11 For it is written, “‘As I live,’ says the Lord, ‘to me every knee will bow. Every tongue will confess to God.’”
12 这样看来，我们各人必要将自己的事在神面前说明。
12 So then each one of us will give account of himself to God.

背景 Background. Paul writes to house churches in Rome divided between the “strong” (mostly Gentile believers who eat anything and treat all days alike) and the 信心软弱的 “weak in faith” (mostly Jewish-background believers who avoid meat — possibly idol-tainted or non-kosher — and keep special days). His rule: 接纳 welcome/accept one another; do not 轻看 despise and do not 论断 judge over 所疑惑的事 “disputable matters,” because (1) God has already accepted the other person (v. 3); (2) each is the Lord’s servant, answerable to his own master (v. 4); (3) both sides act “unto the Lord” with thanksgiving (v. 6); (4) living or dying we belong to the Lord, who died and rose to be Lord of all (vv. 7–9); (5) we will all stand before God’s judgment seat (v. 10, quoting 以赛亚 Isa 45:23 in v. 11) and give account of ourselves — not of each other (v. 12). This is the “bear with one another” (彼此包容) of the sermon text.

马太福音 Matthew 18:21–35 — 不饶恕人的仆人 The unforgiving servant ↑

21 那时，彼得进前来，对耶稣说：「主啊，我弟兄得罪我，我当饶恕他几次呢？到七次可以吗？」
21 Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”
22 耶稣说：「我对你说，不是到七次，乃是到七十个七次。
22 Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.
23 天国好像一个王要和他仆人算帐。
23 Therefore the Kingdom of Heaven is like a certain king, who wanted to reconcile accounts with his servants.
24 才算的时候，有人带了一个欠一千万银子的来。
24 When he had begun to reconcile, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents.
25 因为他没有甚么偿还之物，主人吩咐把他和他妻子儿女，并一切所有的都卖了偿还。
25 But because he couldn’t pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, with his wife, his children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.
26 那仆人就俯伏拜他，说：『主啊，宽容我，将来我都要还清。』
26 The servant therefore fell down and knelt before him, saying, ‘Lord, have patience with me, and I will repay you all!’
27 那仆人的主人就动了慈心，把他释放了，并且免了他的债。
27 The lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, released him, and forgave him the debt.
28 「那仆人出来，遇见他的一个同伴欠他十两银子，便揪着他，掐住他的喉咙，说：『你把所欠的还我！』
28 “But that servant went out, and found one of his fellow servants, who owed him one hundred denarii, and he grabbed him, and took him by the throat, saying, ‘Pay me what you owe!’
29 他的同伴就俯伏央求他，说：『宽容我吧，将来我必还清。』
29 “So his fellow servant fell down at his feet and begged him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you!’
30 他不肯，竟去把他下在监里，等他还了所欠的债。
30 He would not, but went and cast him into prison, until he should pay back that which was due.
31 众同伴看见他所做的事就甚忧愁，去把这事都告诉了主人。
31 So when his fellow servants saw what was done, they were exceedingly sorry, and came and told their lord all that was done.
32 于是主人叫了他来，对他说：『你这恶奴才！你央求我，我就把你所欠的都免了，
32 Then his lord called him in, and said to him, ‘You wicked servant! I forgave you all that debt, because you begged me.
33 你不应当怜恤你的同伴，像我怜恤你吗？』
33 Shouldn’t you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?’
34 主人就大怒，把他交给掌刑的，等他还清了所欠的债。
34 His lord was angry, and delivered him to the tormentors, until he should pay all that was due to him.
35 你们各人若不从心里饶恕你的弟兄，我天父也要这样待你们了。」
35 So my heavenly Father will also do to you, if you don’t each forgive your brother from your hearts for his misdeeds.”

背景 Background. This follows Jesus’ teaching on how to deal with a brother who sins against you (18:15–20). 彼得 (Peter) offers “seven times” — generous by rabbinic standards (three was typical). Jesus’ “seventy times seven” (七十个七次) deliberately reverses 拉麦 Lamech’s boast of unlimited vengeance in Genesis 4:24 (“seventy-sevenfold”): unlimited revenge becomes unlimited forgiveness. The parable’s numbers are the point. The first servant owes 10,000 talents (万他连得; CUV renders it 一千万银子): one talent ≈ 6,000 denarii ≈ 20 years’ wages, so the debt is roughly 200,000 years of labor — an absurd, unpayable sum (all of Herod’s yearly tax revenue was about 900 talents). The master 动了慈心 “was moved with compassion” and simply cancelled it. The fellow servant owes 100 denarii (十两银子) — about three months’ wages: real money, but about one six-hundred-thousandth of what was forgiven. The forgiven man then refuses mercy, and the master’s forgiveness is revoked (v. 34). Verse 35 is the sting: 从心里饶恕 “forgive from the heart.” Forgiveness received must become forgiveness given — the same logic as the Lord’s Prayer later in the service (免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债).

9 · 读经 Sermon Text — 歌罗西书 Colossians 3:12–17 · 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: The sermon text in one line: identity (chosen, holy, beloved) → character (compassion … forgiveness … love over all) → community (peace as referee, the word in song, everything with thanks).

12 所以，你们既是神的选民，圣洁蒙爱的人，就要存怜悯、恩慈、谦虚、温柔、忍耐的心。
12 Put on therefore, as God’s chosen ones, holy and beloved, a heart of compassion, kindness, lowliness, humility, and perseverance;
13 倘若这人与那人有嫌隙，总要彼此包容，彼此饶恕；主怎样饶恕了你们，你们也要怎样饶恕人。
13 bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
14 在这一切之外，要存着爱心，爱心就是联络全德的。
14 Above all these things, walk in love, which is the bond of perfection.
15 又要叫基督的平安在你们心里作主；你们也为此蒙召，归为一体；且要存感谢的心。
15 And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to which also you were called in one body; and be thankful.
16 当用各样的智慧，把基督的道理丰丰富富地存在心里，用诗章、颂词、灵歌，彼此教导，互相劝戒，心被恩感，歌颂神。
16 Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
17 无论做甚么，或说话或行事，都要奉主耶稣的名，藉着他感谢父神。
17 Whatever you do, in word or in deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father, through him.

背景 Background. Paul (with Timothy) writes to the church at 歌罗西 (Colossae, in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor), c. AD 60–62, probably from prison. Chapters 1–2 are doctrine (Christ supreme over everything); chapter 3 turns to practice: “since you have been raised with Christ” (3:1). Verses 5–11 say 脱去 take off the old self’s vices; verses 12–17 say 穿上 put on the new — clothing imagery (the CUV’s 存 in v. 12 is literally 穿 “put on,” as the marginal note says; think of changing garments at baptism). Verse 12 gives the identity: 选民 chosen, 圣洁 holy, 蒙爱 beloved — Israel’s own titles (申 Deut 7:6–8) now applied to a mixed Jewish-Gentile church. Then five virtues, all qualities of Christ himself: 怜悯 compassion (lit. “bowels of mercy”), 恩慈 kindness, 谦虚 humility, 温柔 gentleness, 忍耐 patience; plus 包容 bearing with, and 饶恕 forgiving — “as the Lord forgave you” (the Greek verb is charizomai, to forgive as a free gift of grace). Over everything, 爱心 love, “the bond of perfection” (联络全德 — the belt or outer garment that holds all the others together). Then three community rules (vv. 15–17): let the 平安 peace of Christ rule (作主 — the Greek word means to act as umpire or referee) in your hearts, for you were called into 一体 one body; let the 基督的道理 word of Christ dwell richly, teaching and admonishing one another with 诗章、颂词、灵歌 psalms, hymns and spiritual songs — congregational singing as mutual teaching, a verse every church musician loves; and do everything 奉主耶稣的名 in the name of the Lord Jesus. 感谢 thanksgiving appears three times in three verses (15, 16, 17). Parallel passage: 以弗所书 Ephesians 4:1–3 and 5:19–20.

10 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 250《我属耶稣歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Sung between the readings and the sermon: the forgiven person’s response is to draw nearer — the refrain goes to 受死圣架 “the cross where Thou hast died”, where the unpayable debt of Matthew 18 was cancelled (Col 2:14: he cancelled the record of debt, nailing it to the cross).

♪ 五线谱 score →

“I Am Thine, O Lord” (Draw Me Nearer). Words by Fanny J. Crosby (1820–1915), the blind American hymn-writer, written in 1875 at the Cincinnati home of William H. Doane, who composed the tune the same year; inspired by 希伯来书 Hebrews 10:22, “let us draw near.” Section: 信徒灵修·念主恩爱 (Devotion — remembering the Lord’s love). A-flat major, 4/4.

1. 我乃属耶稣，我听闻主声，主恩爱充满我心；今求赐信心，靠赖主膀臂，常与主相近相亲。
2. 今归主为圣，专为主所用，每日蒙新赐天恩；信望爱日增，口不住称颂，按主旨意度一生。
3. 恩座前祈祷，与我主亲近，似良友亲密相交；心喜乐难言，真得福无尽，主恩甜美无限好。
4. 何其深主爱！我无法测度，直到与主面对面；何等大喜乐！我难以述说，直到安息主怀间。
副歌 Refrain: 更亲近主，亲近我恩主，来到主受死圣架！更亲近主，近主，亲近我恩主，到主流血宝架下！阿们。

1. I am Thine, O Lord, I have heard Thy voice, and it told Thy love to me; but I long to rise in the arms of faith and be closer drawn to Thee.
2. Consecrate me now to Thy service, Lord, by the power of grace divine; let my soul look up with a steadfast hope, and my will be lost in Thine.
3. O the pure delight of a single hour that before Thy throne I spend, when I kneel in prayer, and with Thee, my God, I commune as friend with friend!
4. There are depths of love that I cannot know till I cross the narrow sea; there are heights of joy that I may not reach till I rest in peace with Thee.
Refrain: Draw me nearer, nearer, blessed Lord, to the cross where Thou hast died; draw me nearer, nearer, nearer, blessed Lord, to Thy precious, bleeding side.

11 · 证道 Sermon —《上帝选民该有的生活样式》· 彭金文 牧师 · 众坐·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: Expect the central claim to be that forgiveness is not a feeling but the clothing of God’s people (穿上 put it on) — because you are chosen, you forgive as you were forgiven.

“The Way of Life God’s Chosen People Ought to Have” (上帝 God · 选民 chosen people · 该有的 that they ought to have · 生活样式 pattern/style of life). Text: Colossians 3:12–17.

证道大纲 Sermon outline (from the bulletin):

一、要认识我们的身份是神的选民 (12a节)
1. Recognize our identity (身份): we are God’s chosen people (v. 12a).
二、要知道神的选民该有什么品格 (12b–14节)
2. Know what character (品格) God’s chosen people should have (vv. 12b–14).
三、要遵行团契生活中相处的原则 (15–17节)
3. Practice the principles for living together (相处的原则) in the life of the fellowship (团契) (vv. 15–17).

What to expect under each point. Point 1 — the indicative before the imperative: before Paul asks for anything he tells the Colossians who they already are (chosen, holy, loved) — 身份 identity grounds 行为 behaviour. Expect references to Israel as 选民 and to 彼得前书 1 Peter 2:9 (“a chosen people, a royal priesthood”). Point 2 — the five virtues, then bearing with and forgiving one another “as the Lord forgave you” (the link to Joseph and the unforgiving servant), and love as the belt over all. Point 3 — three principles for the 团契 community: Christ’s peace as referee in conflicts (v. 15), the word of Christ dwelling richly through teaching and singing (v. 16), and doing everything in Jesus’ name with thanksgiving (v. 17).

See 讲道关键词 Sermon key words in the phrases section below.

12 · 堂务报告 Announcements — 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: “One body” (Col 3:15) in practice: the week’s meetings, visits and needs.

Church business: the week’s meetings, evening service at 香榭丽都, visitation, etc. There is no offering item in this order; Three-Self churches usually have 奉献箱 offering boxes at the doors instead.

13 · 欢迎第一次来的朋友 Welcome to First-Time Visitors — 众坐 ↑

主题 Theme: Col 3:11, the verse just before the text: in Christ “there is no Greek or Jew, … but Christ is all and in all” — a visitor from abroad is exactly who that verse welcomes.

Visitors are usually asked to stand (or raise a hand) and are welcomed with applause; sometimes an usher asks your name or the congregation sings a short welcome. A smile, a nod, and 谢谢 / 主内平安 is plenty. You may be handed a welcome card (欢迎卡) or asked 从哪里来 “where are you from?”

14 · 祷告 Prayer — 为有需要者祷告 · 众坐·安静 ↑

主题 Theme: 怜悯 compassion (Col 3:12) turned into intercession for the sick and grieving.

Intercessions for those in need (有需要者): the sick (病人), the bereaved, the church and the nation. Seated, in silence; close with 阿们.

15 · 唱诗 Hymn — 赞美诗 357《爱人歌》· 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Whittier’s “to worship rightly is to love each other” is Col 3:12–14 in verse: 哀怜 pity, 彼此相爱 mutual love, and 忿怒的火 the fire of anger trodden out by love (Col 3:8 lists 恼恨 anger and 忿怒 wrath among the clothes to take off).

♪ 五线谱 score →

“O Brother Man, Fold to Thy Heart Thy Brother.” Words by the American Quaker poet and abolitionist John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892), the closing stanzas of his poem “Worship” (1848). Tune by the English organist-composer Joseph Barnby (1838–1896). Chinese by 刘廷芳 (Timothy T. Lew) and 杨荫浏 (later China’s foremost musicologist), 1934, for 普天颂赞. Section: 信徒灵修·忠心服务 (Devotion — faithful service). Whittier’s “to worship rightly is to love each other” is the sermon in one line. G major, 4/4.

1. 弟兄们啊，放开胸怀爱众人，哀怜所在，即主平安所临；彼此相爱，崇拜才能尽虔诚，祈祷颂扬，莫离和颜善行。
2. 因主爱徒，曾经恳切地教训，在主面前，崇拜不算虔诚；除非同心，挽回迷失医伤心，抚孤恤寡，能够守道力行。
3. 恭敬追踪耶稣慈悲的圣范，耶稣圣工，便是一生行善；茫茫世间，化成拜父的圣殿，仁爱人生，化成感谢诗篇。
4. 到那时期，人身桎梏都落下，世界众生，不闻战乐悲笳；忿怒的火，将被爱心所践踏，死灰之中，盛放和平之花。阿们。

1. O brother man, fold to thy heart thy brother; where pity dwells, the peace of God is there; to worship rightly is to love each other, each smile a hymn, each kindly deed a prayer.
2. For he whom Jesus loved hath truly spoken: the holier worship which he deigns to bless restores the lost, and binds the spirit broken, and feeds the widow and the fatherless.
3. Follow with reverent steps the great example of him whose holy work was doing good; so shall the wide earth seem our Father’s temple, each loving life a psalm of gratitude.
4. Then shall all shackles fall; the stormy clangor of wild war music o’er the earth shall cease; love shall tread out the baleful fire of anger, and in its ashes plant the tree of peace.

16 · 主祷文 The Lord’s Prayer — 马太福音 Matthew 6:9–13 · 众立·同诵 ↑

主题 Theme: 免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债 — the petition Matthew 18:21–35 was told to explain (compare 18:27 免了他的债 “forgave him the debt”).

Recited together in the 和合本 wording (also hymnal 394). Note the petition that ties the whole service together: 免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债 — forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

我们在天上的父，愿人都尊你的名为圣。愿你的国降临，愿你的旨意行在地上，如同行在天上。我们日用的饮食，今日赐给我们。免我们的债，如同我们免了人的债。不叫我们遇见试探，救我们脱离凶恶。因为国度、权柄、荣耀，全是你的，直到永远。阿们。

Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name. Your kingdom come, your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us today our daily bread. Forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever. Amen.

17 · 祝福 Benediction — 众立 ↑

主题 Theme: The Aaronic blessing ends with 平安 peace — “let the peace of Christ rule in your hearts” (Col 3:15).

The pastor’s blessing, usually one of these two:

民数记 Numbers 6:24–26 (亚伦的祝福 Aaronic blessing): 愿耶和华赐福给你，保护你。愿耶和华使他的脸光照你，赐恩给你。愿耶和华向你仰脸，赐你平安。
The Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine on you and be gracious to you; the Lord lift up his countenance on you and give you peace.

哥林多后书 2 Corinthians 13:14: 愿主耶稣基督的恩惠、神的慈爱、圣灵的感动，常与你们众人同在！
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

18 · 阿们颂 Amen — 众立·同唱 ↑

主题 Theme: Amen — Hebrew “firm, true, so be it.” Col 3:17: whatever you do, in word or deed, do it in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks.

The sung Amen (hymnal 400 offers two-, three-, four-fold [Neukomm] and a twelve-fold Amen by 关筑声, 1982); the three-fold Amen is the usual one. 阿们，阿们，阿们。 Then the choir and ministers recess; people greet one another — 主内平安 / 感谢主 (thank the Lord).
